claims.claim: (1a) Query.setModel exists and switches the model mid-turn
claims.detail: `setModel(model?: string): Promise<void>`, streaming-input mode only. It takes effect during the current turn: the response already being generated finishes on the old model, and the next model call uses the new one. Before CC v2.1.212 the switch waited for the next turn. Subagents keep their own model. Passing undefined or 'default' resets to Claude Code's default model. Since SDK 0.3.268 the CLI checks an unknown id with the API at the first switch. A PreModelSwitch hook fires with source 'sdk'; if it returns 'ask', a headless session refuses the switch. Each model has its own prompt cache, so every Haiku<->Opus swap re-reads the whole context with no cache hits.

claims.claim: (1b) Query.applyFlagSettings({effortLevel, model}): effort applies from the next turn, model during the current turn
claims.detail: `applyFlagSettings(settings: { [K in keyof Settings]?: K extends 'effortLevel' ? EffortLevel | null : Settings[K] | null }): Promise<void>`, streaming-input mode only, and it shallow-merges top-level keys. Applied on the next turn: effortLevel, ultracode, permissions, hooks, skillOverrides, fastMode, agent. Applied during the current turn: model (same as setModel). System-prompt options have no effect mid-session. Passing null resets effortLevel to the model's default effort and model to Claude Code's default model, not settings.model. effortLevel also accepts 'max', session-only. Only the TypeScript signature was checked; the Python equivalent was not.

claims.claim: (1c) An explicit session effort (Options.effort / --effort) carries over to the new model after setModel
claims.detail: The documented effort order is: CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL / --effort / /effort first, then saved per-model settings (modelSettings.<model>.effortLevel, top-level effortLevel), then the model default (Opus 5.5 / Haiku 5.5 default to 'medium'). Since CC 2.1.251, effort is saved per model 'so each model keeps its own setting when you switch'. No source says whether an explicit session level survives a setModel. Safe pattern: call `applyFlagSettings({ model, effortLevel })` on every swap, and remember the effort only lands on the next turn. Note that CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL in the child env overrides everything.

claims.claim: (1d) T3 Code closes and re-opens the query (resume) when model or effort changes
claims.detail: In compileClaudeModelSelection, `queryIdentity: JSON.stringify({ apiModelId, effort: effort ?? null, settings })`. The adapter reuses a live query only when `existing.selectionKey === compiledSelection.queryIdentity`; otherwise it opens a new query with resume. Comments note that a new selection kills background shells and agents. T3 wraps `setModel` in its runner but does not use it for selection changes.

claims.claim: (2a) Query.setMcpServers attaches and detaches stdio and in-process SDK MCP servers mid-session

claims.claim: (3a) canUseTool returning {behavior:'allow', updatedInput} can rewrite a Bash command
claims.detail: `PermissionResult = { behavior:'allow'; updatedInput?: Record<string,unknown>; updatedPermissions?: PermissionUpdate[]; toolUseID?; decisionClassification? } | { behavior:'deny'; message: string; interrupt?; toolUseID?; decisionClassification? }`. claims.claim: (5a) additionalDirectories and working directories scope Read/Edit/Write
claims.detail: `additionalDirectories?: string[]` is passed as `--add-dir` and also loads that directory's skills, commands and agents under the 'project' source. Files in working dirs are readable without prompts; edits follow the permission mode, so in 'default' mode an edit outside them reaches canUseTool, where you can deny it. `Settings.permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories?: boolean` refuses Read, Grep, Glob and LSP outside the working dirs in every mode. claims.claim: (5b) Permission rules passed through Options.settings restrict file tools to directories
claims.detail: `settings?: string | Settings` goes into the flag layer (same as --settings), with `permissions: { allow?, deny?, ask?, defaultMode?, additionalDirectories?, blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories? }`. Use `Edit(path)` and `Read(path)` rules only: Edit covers Write and NotebookEdit, and a `Write(path)` rule is never consulted. Use `//abs/path/**` for absolute paths, because a single leading `/` anchors at the settings source; for an inline object the anchor is not documented, so prefer `//`. Deny beats allow. Read/Edit deny rules also hit recognized Bash file commands (cat, head, sed, tee, redirections) but NOT arbitrary subprocesses; only the sandbox enforces at OS level.

claims.claim: (8) Per-session memory and CPU footprint, and limits for 4-8 concurrent sessions
claims.detail: One query() = one claude subprocess. Anthropic's sizing guidance is '1 GiB RAM, 5 GiB disk, and 1 CPU per agent' as a starting floor; memory grows with session length and tool activity, so measure peak RSS and recycle long sessions. Local measurement on this Mac: native claude 2.1.289/2.1.291 processes at 105-342 MB RSS and 0-6% CPU. 8 sessions is about 1-3 GB typical (budget 8 GiB worst case), plus each session's stdio MCP children. RAM is not the binding limit on 48 GB; the subscription usage window is. Use `rate_limit_event` messages (`SDKRateLimitInfo { status:'allowed'|'allowed_warning'|'rejected', resetsAt?, rateLimitType?: 'five_hour'|'seven_day'|'seven_day_opus'|..., utilization? }`) for the concurrency governor.

claims.claim: (9) SDKUserMessage priority 'now'/'next'/'later' and shouldQuery semantics
claims.detail: `priority?: 'now'|'next'|'later'`. 'next' (or no field): read in the same turn once the running tool calls finish, or starts the next turn if the turn ends first. 'later': held until the turn ends, then sent as a new turn. 'now' with `origin:{kind:'human'}` (CC >= 2.1.286): movable work (shell, subagents, MCP calls, and on 2.1.287+ WebFetch/WebSearch) goes to the background and the message joins the turn; otherwise the turn is interrupted. 'now' without human origin interrupts the turn. `shouldQuery: false`: appended to the transcript with no model call and merged into the next user message that does query. `origin` is human, channel with server, or peer.

designImplications: Do the model/effort swap at a turn boundary: when the sit_at_pc tool succeeds, call `applyFlagSettings({ model: 'opus', effortLevel: 'medium' })`, have the tool result tell the agent to end its turn, and have the orchestrator start the next turn ('PC acquired') so the effort lands. Do the reverse on stand-up. Debounce swaps, because each one re-reads the whole context uncached on the other model. T3-style close+resume is the fallback if mid-session swapping misbehaves.

Pass `settingSources: []`, explicit `model`/`effort`, `permissionMode: 'default'` and `strictMcpConfig: true`. Otherwise the user's ~/.claude/settings.json (model opus, effortLevel xhigh, per-model effort, any PreModelSwitch hooks) leaks into agents and can block or alter swaps.

Use the SDK-bundled 2.1.293 binary (omit pathToClaudeCodeExecutable), or check `supportedModels()` at boot and refuse to start if the haiku row does not resolve to claude-haiku-5-5. The local CLI 2.1.284 cannot run Haiku 5.5. Keychain auth is unaffected by the choice as long as HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR are left alone.

Avoid setMcpServers churn. Register one in-process SDK MCP server (e.g. 'pc', `alwaysLoad: true`) at query start. Its screenshot/click/type/key/scroll/bash/read/write tools route to whichever PC the agent currently occupies, and return an error such as 'not seated at a PC' otherwise. The tool list stays stable (cache intact, no ToolSearch). If you do use `cua mcp` stdio per PC, always pass the FULL server map, including the minecraft SDK server, because setMcpServers replaces the set.

No host shell: set `disallowedTools: ['Bash']` and `toolAliases: { Bash: 'mcp__pc__bash' }`. Implement the PC bash tool with persistent cwd and env per agent+PC, a timeout, background jobs and output truncation, since those built-in features are lost. Don't rely on CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL or CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL_PREFIX.

File tools: built-in Read/Edit/Write only see the host filesystem. Either disallow them and alias them to PC-side MCP file tools, or, for Linux containers, bind-mount each chosen host folder at the IDENTICAL absolute path inside the container. Then set cwd/additionalDirectories to those mounts, `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories: true`, and deny edits outside via canUseTool. macOS Lume shares mount under a different path, so they need the MCP route.
Use a PreToolUse hook callback, not canUseTool, as the universal guard and rewriter: it runs on every call, including auto-approved ones. Keep canUseTool for the human-in-the-loop prompts.

Hold AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode as pending canUseTool promises until the player answers via the agent's in-world UI, and honour `options.signal`. Answer with `{ questions, answers: { [question]: label } }`, joining multi-select labels with ', '. For ExitPlanMode read `input.plan` and, on approval, explicitly set the next permission mode. Expect plan-mode turns on Haiku to possibly run on Sonnet.

Inject game events as SDKUserMessages: ambient telemetry with `shouldQuery: false`; normal events with 'next'; emergencies (taking damage, player died, kicked off PC) with 'now' to interrupt; low-priority chatter with 'later'.

Concurrency governor: about 4 agents with active turns at a time (idle sessions cost only ~150-350 MB). Throttle or pause new turns from `rate_limit_event` utilization (five_hour / seven_day) and pause on status 'rejected'. RAM budget is about 1 GiB per agent plus about 4 GiB per Linux PC container.

Build the child env from a scrubbed copy of process.env: drop /^(ANTHROPIC_|CLAUDE|MCP_)/ and DISABLE_MICROCOMPACT, keep HOME and PATH, and add CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP='minevibe/x'. Decide CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY per the memory-persistence design: auto memory loads regardless of settingSources.

Agent memory across world resets can use persisted sessions (`resume: sessionId`, or a fresh session seeded with a summary) and per-agent cwd/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR-free project dirs. Pick a stable per-agent `cwd` so ~/.claude/projects/<dir> transcripts and memory group per agent.

claims.claim: How cua applies CPU/memory limits to local containers
claims.detail: bollard HostConfig sets nano_cpus = cpus*1e9 (capped at the engine's CPUs), memory = memory_mb MiB (hard limit), shm_size = half of memory clamped to 64 MiB..2 GiB. Ports are published on 127.0.0.1 with a random host port. It sets no binds or mounts. cap_add SYS_ADMIN applies only under runsc.

claims.claim: Host folder bind mounts are supported through cua (SDK/CLI)
claims.detail: SandboxCreateOptions, SpaceCreateOptions and `cua sb create` have no mount, volume or shared-dir field, and the container HostConfig has no binds or mounts. The only file paths are: Cua Volume (FSL FUSE drive, mountable only in gVisor sandboxes per test `only_gvisor_sandboxes_can_mount_the_volume`), `Space.upload/download/sendFile/write`, `cua sb cp`, and the HTML5 viewer's `--files` upload/folder sharing.
claims.source: @trycua/cua d.ts; cua-vmm/src/container/mod.rs; docs cua-cli reference sandbox.mdx/sandbox-access.mdx

claims.claim: Raw 'docker run -v … ghcr.io/trycua/linux:24.04' works and can be driven by the SDK
claims.detail: The image is a plain OCI rootfs with CMD ['/opt/cua/desktop/entrypoint.sh'] (supervisord as PID 1), no USER, Env DISPLAY=:1 CUA_X_SERVER=xvfb, EXPOSE 3211/tcp 3212/udp 18080/tcp, and a HEALTHCHECK. The repo's own smoke test runs `docker run -d --name N --runtime=runc --shm-size=512m --memory=4g --memory-swap=4g -e CUA_ENV_TOKEN=$TOKEN -p 127.0.0.1::3211 IMAGE`. Add `-v ~/Code/foo:/home/cua/work/foo` (standard Docker, not tested by cua). Connect from Node with `embedded().spacesd('http://127.0.0.1:<port>', token)` or `embedded().sandboxes().connectUrl(url, token, name)` (location 'direct'). Such containers do not appear in `cua sb ls`.

claims.claim: File ownership/permissions of OrbStack bind mounts for container uid 1000 (cua user)
claims.detail: OrbStack docs say bind mounts 'work seamlessly as they would on Linux' over VirtioFS, and recommend volumes for speed. They do not document uid mapping. Secondary sources say OrbStack presents bind-mounted files as owned by whichever uid asks. Needs a spike: write as uid 1000 and check host ownership.

claims.claim: Lume shared directories (--shared-dir / VirtioFS) and guest mount path
claims.detail: CLI: `lume run <vm> --shared-dir PATH[:ro|:rw]` (repeatable). REST: `POST /lume/vms/:name/run` with body `sharedDirectories: [{hostPath, readOnly}]`; the host path must exist. Every share uses tag VZVirtioFileSystemDeviceConfiguration.macOSGuestAutomountTag ('com.apple.virtio-fs.automount') in one VZMultipleDirectoryShare, so a macOS guest sees each directory at `/Volumes/My Shared Files/<basename>` (duplicate names get ' (2)'). A Linux guest has to mount that tag itself (mount -t virtiofs). The REST API has no endpoint to add a share to a running VM; only the native viewer's 'Share Folder' does that, for one run.

claims.claim: cua-created macOS sandboxes can get user host-folder shares
claims.detail: cua's Lume backend fills shared_directories with only its setup share (~/.cua/vmm/lume/<name>/setup with env-token, read-only). The guest reads `/Volumes/My Shared Files/setup/env-token` and persists it to ~/.cua/spacesd/token. A restart reuses that share, and there is no user-share option. Workaround (uncertain): MineVibe drives `lume run`/REST itself, passing the setup dir plus repo dirs, or relies on the persisted guest token.

claims.claim: Unary screenshot RPC from Node: JPEG/quality/max_dimension/include_cursor, returns scale/logical bounds
claims.detail: `SpacesdClient.screenshot({ format: ImageFormat.Jpeg, quality: 1-100, maxDimension, includeCursor })` returns `Screenshot { image: ArrayBuffer, format, width, height, scale, screenshotId }`. Proto ScreenshotRequest takes display_id|window, region, format, quality (0 means 80), max_dimension and include_cursor. ScreenshotResponse adds native_size, logical_bounds, display_id and captured_at. `Space.screenshot(opts)` and `Space.thumbnail(maxAgeMs)` (cached small JPEG) also exist.

claims.claim: WebP screenshots are supported
claims.detail: spacesd's encode_image says 'WebP encoding is not bundled; PNG is returned and reported'. JPEG uses the pure-Rust `image` crate JpegEncoder.

claims.claim: Realistic screenshot-polling fps
claims.detail: No published benchmark. On Linux each Screenshot call runs `grab_once()`, which builds a new X11 Grabber connection with an XShm grab, then does a BGRA→RGB swap and a CPU JPEG encode in Rust. Expect roughly 5-15 fps per PC at 1280x800, as an estimate only. Measure in a spike. For seated 30 fps use StreamService instead.

claims.claim: StreamService/OpenMedia supports bgra and png codecs for Linux desktop streaming
claims.detail: Split answer. BGRA works on Linux; PNG does not. Linux `formats()` returns [H264AnnexB, Bgra8] and ListTargets advertises [H264, BGRA]. select_codec walks the client's list in order, so requesting only PNG fails with FailedPrecondition 'no acceptable codec', while [png, bgra] falls back to BGRA. The proto calls BGRA 'Raw top-down BGRA, tightly packed. Loopback / debugging only'. The Linux X11 capture is XDamage-gated (a static screen costs about nothing), downscales BGRA to max_dimension, and clamps max_fps to 1..120 (0 means 30). bitrate_kbps 250..100000 applies to H.264 only. A BGRA frame at 1280x800 is about 4.1 MB, so 30 fps is about 123 MB/s over loopback; at 960x600 about 69 MB/s.
claims.source: libs/cua-spacesd/crates/cua-spacesd-desktop/src/lib.rs L1640-1668; grpc/stream.rs L254, L311-320; cua-spacesd-session/src/media/session.rs L388-400, L518-529; linux_stream.rs; libs/cua/proto/cua/env/v1/stream.proto

claims.claim: Node SDK media API delivers decoded frames (so Node/JVM can avoid H.264 decoding via the SDK)
claims.detail: The open-source npm SDK delivers encoded frames only: `SpacesdClient.openMedia(MediaOpenOptions{display?, windowHandle?, maxFps, maxDimension, audio, disableVideo, requestJson?}, FrameSink{onFrame(VideoFrame{sequence, keyframe, width, height, captureTimestampUs, codecEpoch, geometryEpoch, data, headerJson}), onEvent})`. MediaOpenOptions has no codecs field, so BGRA must be requested through the escape hatch `requestJson: '{"codecs":["MEDIA_CODEC_BGRA"]}'`. Decoded BGRA/PCM (`spacesd_open_media_decoded`) is Swift-only FSL (cua-spaces-ffi) and is not in npm 0.4.1. examples/streaming/typescript-node/README mentions `openMediaDecodedWithAudio`, but that is not in the published typings or the TS source on main. `Space.openStream(SpaceStreamOptions{codecs:['h264'|'bgra'|'png'], maxFps, policy})` mints a ticket and wsUrl that another client can attach to.

claims.claim: A JVM client can attach to the media socket directly with a ticket (avoiding Node relaying frames)
claims.detail: Documented wire: WebSocket `/media?ticket=<t>` on port 3211, or subprotocols `rcdp.v2` plus `cua.ticket.<t>`. The ticket is validated at upgrade (401/410), TTL 60 s default and 10 min max, and the root token never goes on the socket. Control messages are JSON `{type,payload}`. Video packets are length-prefixed (`header_len: u32`, `payload_len: u32`, big-endian) with a JSON header, and flow control keeps only the latest frame. MEDIA.md also describes v2 fragments (RVD2/RAU2 magic), so a hand-written Java client needs a spike. The Kotlin UniFFI binding (package ai.cua.sdk, JNA) exists, but 'no Gradle package or release artifact is produced yet' and as checked in it does not compile without a patch.

claims.claim: Pointer/keyboard input RPCs from Node, including key down/up and named keys
claims.detail: Typed SpacesdClient methods: click(x,y), doubleClick, rightClick, moveTo, drag(fx,fy,tx,ty), scroll(dx,dy) (in lines), typeText, press(key), hotkey(keys[]), cursorPosition, getClipboard/setClipboard. Down/up are reachable only through proto3 JSON: `pointerJson('{"down":{"button":"MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT"}}')` (actions click/move/down/up/drag/scroll; buttons LEFT/RIGHT/MIDDLE/BACK/FORWARD; ScrollUnit LINE/PIXEL; modifiers) and `keyboardJson('{"down":{"key":{"named":"KEY_SHIFT"}}}')` (actions type/press/hotkey/down/up; KeyInput = named Key enum or a single `character`). KeySpec.parse accepts KEY_* names, their suffix in any case, aliases ctrl, option/opt, cmd/command/super/win, up/down/left/right, esc, return, del, or one character. InputTarget supports COORDINATE_SPACE_SCREENSHOT with screenshot_id. Media-plane input is `MediaSession.sendControl(json)` and needs SessionPolicy ALLOW_ACTIVATION.
claims.source: computer.proto (PointerRequest, KeyboardRequest, KeyInput, Key enum); libs/cua/crates/cua-spacesd-client/src/computer.rs L66-110; @trycua/cua d.ts SpacesdClientLike

claims.claim: No documented multi-controller locking
claims.detail: Only the media plane has input leases: 'at most one principal drives a given window at a time', with an idle-expiring lease that releases held keys on handover. Unary ComputerService Pointer/Keyboard calls have no occupancy lock, so MineVibe must enforce one occupant per PC itself.

claims.claim: 'cua mcp --sandbox <name>' tool list includes computer_shell
claims.detail: Exact computer tools: computer_screenshot (PNG, long edge at most 1200 px, sets the coordinate space), computer_click, computer_double_click, computer_move_cursor, computer_mouse_down, computer_mouse_up, computer_type, computer_key, computer_key_down, computer_key_up, computer_hotkey ('ctrl+c' joined by +), computer_scroll, computer_drag, computer_clipboard_get/_set, computer_file_read/_write/_list, computer_shell (sh -c, 120 s timeout), computer_window_list/open/focus/unfocus/minimize/maximize/close/resize/move/get_info, computer_launch, computer_get_screen_size, computer_get_cursor_position, computer_get_current_window, computer_get_accessibility_tree, computer_accessibility_act. claims.claim: '--sandbox' pins an MCP instance to one sandbox
claims.detail: `--sandbox` (CUA_SANDBOX) is only the default target. `Server::target()` reads `a["sandbox"]` from each tool call first, so any call can drive another sandbox by name or ref ('each call can pass sandbox').

claims.claim: Multiple 'cua mcp' instances for different sandboxes can run concurrently
claims.detail: Each instance is a separate stdio process using the embedded runtime, or the `cua daemon` when ~/.cua/daemon.json exists. State files are written by atomic rename, and each process keeps its own screenshot coordinate mapping per sandbox. There is no explicit lock, and concurrency is not documented or tested. Docs recommend `cua daemon mcp` 'so several agents share Spaces, streams and sandboxes'.

claims.claim: spacesd serves an HTTP MCP endpoint at /mcp
claims.detail: Streamable-HTTP MCP over the in-process cua-driver tool registry, with bearer auth, Mcp-Session-Id sessions, and an optional `X-Cua-Agent-Session` header (one driver session and cursor per agent; DELETE /mcp ends it). It is served from inside the guest, so it is inherently bound to that one PC. Its tool names are cua-driver's, not the `computer_*` set. Whether it includes a shell tool was not verified.

claims.claim: Running shell commands in a sandbox from the host
claims.detail: CLI: `cua sb exec NAME -- cmd` (one sh -c line, exits with the command's status; Lume without spacesd uses lume ssh) and `cua sb shell NAME` (PTY, --cols/--rows). SDK: `SpacesdClient.sh(line, timeoutMs)`, `run(SpacesdCommand)`, `spawn(SpacesdCommand{program, args, env, cwd, user, timeoutMs, tag, stdin, pty:{cols,rows}})` returning SpacesdProcess (writeStdin, writePty, resize, signal, kill, wait, nextEvent, detach), and `attach(pid, tag, replay)` to reattach by tag. Also `Space.bash(cmd, timeoutMs)`. Raw: `docker exec -u cua <ctr> desktop-env <cmd>` (the image's desktop-env script loads DISPLAY and the session bus and drops to user cua).

claims.claim: A visible terminal (tmux attached in an XFCE terminal) is feasible in linux:24.04
claims.detail: xfce4-terminal is installed. tmux is not: it is absent from the Dockerfile apt list and the full-tier software manifest. User cua (uid 1000) has `NOPASSWD:ALL` sudo, so `sudo apt-get install -y tmux` at runtime or a derived image both work. Then spawn `xfce4-terminal -e 'tmux new -A -s agent'` on DISPLAY :1 and run agent commands in that session. xdotool, wmctrl, xclip and imagemagick are also present.

claims.claim: Persistence semantics across stop/start
claims.detail: Local container: suspend = `docker pause` (memory kept and still occupies RAM; becomes a plain stop if OrbStack or the Mac restarts). resume = unpause, or `docker start` when stopped. The writable layer survives stop/start and is lost on delete. Port bindings are fixed at create; cua recreates the container from a `docker commit` if ports change. Lume: 'Lume has no in-memory pause', so suspend = stop (disk kept) and resume boots it. macOS bases are pulled once into a stopped `cua-base-<sha12>` VM and cloned per sandbox with APFS clonefile. Local sandboxes have no TTL and run until deleted.

claims.claim: cua is stable enough to track 'latest'
claims.detail: Releases between 2026-10-02 and 10-08 include cua-sdk 0.3.0→0.3.1→0.4.0→0.4.1, cua-spacesd 0.1.2→0.5.3 (about 10 releases), cua-spaces 0.2.0→0.7.2, and lume-v0.6.1 plus nightlies. Image tags are rebuilt every few days.

designImplications: Linux PCs on this Mac run as runc containers inside OrbStack's VM, not gVisor. Treat docker info MemTotal (about 15.66 GiB; OrbStack memory_mib=16384) and NCPU=18 as the Linux-PC capacity budget for the resource indicator. Lume macOS VMs draw from the remaining host RAM (48 GiB total) and are capped at 2. Subtract other running containers (one is in a restart loop now).

Mounts are fixed at container create and cua cannot set them. Let the agentic server own Linux PC containers directly (dockerode or docker CLI): `docker run -d --runtime=runc --memory=… --memory-swap=… --cpus=… --shm-size=… -e CUA_ENV_TOKEN=… -p 127.0.0.1::3211 -v <host repo>:/home/cua/work/<name> -v minevibe-<pc>-home:/home/cua <pinned digest>`, labelled minevibe.pc=<id>. Then connect with `embedded().spacesd(url, token)` or `sandboxes().connectUrl`. Changing mounts means recreating the container, so keep state in a named volume. Use the cua SDK for create/suspend/resume only for PCs that need no mounts.

Build a thin derived image FROM ghcr.io/trycua/linux@sha256:<digest> that adds tmux (and optionally the agent tooling). Pin both the image digest and @trycua/cua@0.4.1 exactly; cua ships several releases a day.

Monitor video: for the seated PC, open StreamService with codecs [BGRA] (through MediaOpenOptions.requestJson) at max_dimension around 960-1280 and max_fps 30. The capture is XDamage-gated, so idle screens are nearly free. Either forward the BGRA in Node (optionally zstd/lz4) or, after a spike, have the Java mod attach to /media itself with a ticket from Space.openStream / OpenMedia. Never request PNG-only on Linux; it fails. If H.264 is kept, decode in Node with the installed ffmpeg or in Java, because the npm SDK does not decode. For visible-but-unseated monitors, use JPEG screenshots (quality around 60, maxDimension around 640) at 1-2 fps or Space.thumbnail.

Input: map SDL3 key events to proto Key enum names and send them with `keyboardJson({down|up:{key:{named:'KEY_…'}}})` / `pointerJson({down|up|move|scroll})`, so held keys and drags behave like a real keyboard. Track pressed keys per occupant and release all of them on unseat or kick, since unary RPCs have no lease.

Agent tools: do not give agents raw `cua mcp`. Its `sandbox` argument overrides --sandbox, and sandbox_* tools can create or delete PCs, which breaks single occupancy. Register MineVibe's own SDK-MCP tools (createSdkMcpServer) bound to the PC the agent is seated at: screenshot (JPEG, returns scale), click/move/drag/scroll, key_down/up/press/hotkey, type, shell (spawn with PTY and tag inside a tmux session shown in xfce4-terminal), and file read/write. Enable them only while seated, by toggling mcpServers or rejecting in canUseTool. Alternative: point a per-PC HTTP MCP config at that PC's spacesd /mcp with X-Cua-Agent-Session, which is naturally pinned to one PC.
Run one embedded cua runtime inside the Node agentic server, not one `cua mcp` process per agent. Set CUA_TELEMETRY=0 / DO_NOT_TRACK=1 in the server and in spawned agent environments.

Ship cua as an npm dependency of the server (@trycua/cua plus @trycua/cua-darwin-arm64, which also provides the `cua` binary). No Homebrew is needed. cua downloads its pinned built-in Lume on the first macOS create, so the macOS PC's first boot means a ~24 GB download and a sparse 150 GiB disk (199 GiB free now). Gate it behind a confirmation with a progress UI.

macOS PCs with host folders are a stretch goal. cua exposes no share option, so MineVibe would drive `lume run`/REST with `--shared-dir <setup dir containing env-token>` plus repo dirs (guest path /Volumes/My Shared Files/<basename>), or fall back to Space.upload/download sync. Lume 'suspend' is a full stop, so macOS PCs cold-boot on resume. Show that in the UI.

Persistence across a world reset: containers, named volumes and Lume disks survive app restarts (pause becomes stop after an engine restart; resume handles both). Decide explicitly whether a new world reuses the PCs (cheap) or recreates them from the base image. Host-mounted repos always persist.

PC type menu: Linux container (default, fast, arm64-native), macOS (Lume, at most 2, heavy), optional Linux VM (QEMU-HVF/Lume, stronger isolation). Hide Windows, or label it 'emulated, very slow' (amd64 TCG). Skip Android and Omarchy. A 'browser PC' is just the Linux image with Chromium kiosk.

claims.detail: 9.6.0 is the version in the blog, which pairs it with Loom 1.17. The current 26.3 template uses distributionUrl=https://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-9.7.1-bin.zip, and Loom's own dev/1.18 wrapper is 9.7.0. Use Gradle 9.7.1 with Loom 1.18.x.

claims.detail: The example sets options.release=25 and source/targetCompatibility=JavaVersion.VERSION_25. fabric.mod.json declares depends java '>=25', minecraft '~26.3' and fabricloader '>=0.19.5'. The local Temurin 17 cannot compile this or run Loom 1.18.

claims.claim: (2a) Carpet's EntityPlayerMPFake creation for 26.3 uses placeNewPlayer(new FakeClientConnection(SERVERBOUND), fake, CommonListenerCookie).
claims.detail: Carpet tag v26.3 (MIT): `new EntityPlayerMPFake(server, level, profile, ClientInformation.createDefault(), false)` calls super ServerPlayer(MinecraftServer server, ServerLevel level, GameProfile gameProfile, ClientInformation clientInformation). Then `server.getPlayerList().placeNewPlayer(new FakeClientConnection(PacketFlow.SERVERBOUND), instance, new CommonListenerCookie(profile, 0, instance.clientInformation(), false))`. CommonListenerCookie is a record (GameProfile gameProfile, int latency, ClientInformation clientInformation, boolean transferred). FakeClientConnection extends Connection, sets an EmbeddedChannel through an accessor mixin (ClientConnectionInterface.setChannel), and no-ops send(Packet, ChannelFutureListener, boolean), setReadOnly, handleDisconnection, setListenerForServerboundHandshake and setupInboundProtocol. PlayerList_fakePlayersMixin @Redirects `new ServerGamePacketListenerImpl(...)` in placeNewPlayer to NetHandlerPlayServerFake, and `new ServerPlayer(...)` in respawn. GameProfile is now a record: `new GameProfile(UUID,String)`, profile.name(), profile.id().

claims.claim: (2b) How a Carpet fake player handles death and respawn.
claims.detail: EntityPlayerMPFake.die(DamageSource) runs shakeOff(), super.die(cause), setHealth(20), foodData=new FoodData(), then kill(getCombatTracker().getDeathMessage()). kill() schedules connection.onDisconnect(new DisconnectionDetails(reason)) on the next tick, which leads to PlayerList.remove and a playerdata save. The fake is removed and never respawns. Inventory drops through vanilla die unless keepInventory is on. Saved playerdata has health 20, and Carpet's loadPlayerData restores it if the same UUID spawns again.

claims.claim: (2c) EntityPlayerActionPack provides use/attack/jump/drop/swap, setForward/strafing/look/sneak/sprint, and riding.
claims.detail: ActionType has USE, ATTACK, JUMP, DROP_ITEM, DROP_STACK and SWAP_HANDS. Methods include setForward, setStrafing, look(yaw,pitch), lookAt(Vec3), turn, setSneaking, setSprinting, stopMovement, mount(boolean) and dismount(). Movement sets player.zza and player.xxa, and vanilla server-side physics does the rest, so you only supply steering inputs. Caveat: mount() calls player.startRiding(e, true, true), and force=true bypasses canRide/canAddPassenger.

claims.claim: (3a) In hardcore, the local player's death shows a death screen and the player becomes a spectator on respawn.
claims.detail: ClientPacketListener.handlePlayerCombatKill calls gui.setScreen(new DeathScreen(msg, levelData.isHardcore(), player)), or player.respawn() if !shouldShowDeathScreen. The hardcore DeathScreen has 'deathScreen.spectate' ("Spectate World", calls LocalPlayer.respawn()) and 'deathScreen.titleScreen'. The title button exits without confirmation through disconnectWithSavingScreen and then a TitleScreen. The server's ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleClientCommand(PERFORM_RESPAWN) calls respawn(player,false,KILLED) and then, if server.isHardcore(), player.setGameMode(GameType.SPECTATOR). Vanilla never deletes the world. Gui.setScreen re-creates the DeathScreen if a null screen is set while the player is dead.
claims.source: 26.3 client.jar bytecode: ClientPacketListener, DeathScreen, Gui.setScreen, ServerGamePacketListenerImpl

claims.claim: (3b) A mod can replace a hardcore world without showing the title screen (createWorldOpenFlows().createFreshLevel).
claims.detail: All the APIs exist; the full flow has not been tested at runtime. Step 1: `mc.disconnect(Screen screen, boolean keepResourcePacks)` with a GenericMessageScreen. It halts the IntegratedServer and loops renderFrame until isShutdown(), which means the server thread has exited. stopServer closes the LevelStorageAccess before that happens. Step 2: `try(var a = mc.getLevelSource().createAccess(oldId)){ a.deleteLevel(); }`. Step 3: `mc.createWorldOpenFlows().createFreshLevel(String levelId, LevelSettings levelSettings, WorldOptions options, Function<HolderLookup.Provider,WorldDimensions> dimensionsProvider, Screen parentScreen)`. Build the settings with `new LevelSettings(name, GameType.SURVIVAL, new LevelSettings.DifficultySettings(Difficulty.HARD, true /*hardcore*/, false), false, WorldDataConfiguration.DEFAULT)`, `WorldOptions.defaultWithRandomSeed()` and `WorldPresets::createNormalWorldDimensions`. Vanilla does the same delete-then-createFreshLevel in SelectWorldScreen's debug 'recreate' button, using FileUtil.findAvailableName. Alternatives are the public static QuickPlay.connect and WorldOpenFlows.openWorld(String, Runnable). Detect the death with Fabric ServerLivingEntityEvents.ALLOW_DEATH or AFTER_DEATH, or a client mixin on handlePlayerCombatKill.
claims.source: 26.3 client.jar bytecode: Minecraft.disconnect, MinecraftServer.isShutdown/stopServer, WorldOpenFlows, SelectWorldScreen; fabric-api 26.3 ServerLivingEntityEvents.java

claims.claim: (3c) A fake player that dies in a hardcore world becomes a spectator.
claims.detail: The hardcore spectator switch exists only in handleClientCommand(PERFORM_RESPAWN), which a fake player never sends. PlayerList.respawn has no isHardcore check, so a manual PlayerList.respawn would revive the fake in survival. With Carpet's die() override, the fake is removed cleanly through disconnect. For permadeath, also delete its playerdata or use a fresh UUID.
claims.source: 26.3 bytecode (callers of isHardcore: only handleClientCommand, placeNewPlayer, Gui.setScreen, etc.) ; carpet v26.3 EntityPlayerMPFake.die

claims.claim: (4a) LWJGL STB (stb_image) is on the 26.3 classpath and can decode JPEG.
claims.detail: 26.3.json includes org.lwjgl:lwjgl-stb:3.4.3 plus natives-macos-arm64, and NativeImage itself calls org.lwjgl.stb.STBImage.stbi_load_from_memory. To decode JPEG, call STBImage.stbi_load_from_memory(buf, w, h, comp, 4) and wrap the result with the public `new NativeImage(NativeImage.Format.RGBA, width, height, true /*useStbFree*/, MemoryUtil.memAddress(pixels))`. The constructor's parameters are format, width, height, useStbFree, pixels.
claims.source: 26.3.json libraries; client.jar NativeImage bytecode and MethodParameters

claims.claim: (4b) NativeImage.read is PNG-only.
claims.detail: NativeImage.read(ByteBuffer) calls net.minecraft.util.PngInfo.validateHeader(buffer) before STB, so JPEG input fails. The overloads read(InputStream), read(byte[]) and read(ByteBuffer) all route through this check.

claims.claim: (4c) DynamicTexture constructor and upload API in 26.3.
claims.detail: Constructors: DynamicTexture(Supplier<String> label, NativeImage image), which creates the GPU texture and uploads it; DynamicTexture(String label, int width, int height, boolean zero); and DynamicTexture(Supplier<String> label, int width, int height, boolean zero). Methods are upload(), getPixels() and setPixels(NativeImage), which closes the old image while the GPU texture keeps its size. upload() runs RenderSystem.getDevice().createCommandEncoder().writeToTexture(texture, pixels). The texture is GpuFormat.RGBA8_UNORM with sampler SamplerCache.getRepeat(FilterMode.NEAREST), held in the protected field AbstractTexture.sampler. getClampToEdge(FilterMode.LINEAR) is available. The GPU API is now in com.mojang.renderpearl.api.*. Partial updates: CommandEncoder.writeToTexture(GpuTexture destination, NativeImage source, int mipLevel, int depthOrLayer, int destX, int destY) and writeToTexture(GpuTexture destination, ByteBuffer source, int mipLevel, int depthOrLayer, int destX, int destY, int width, int height). Register with TextureManager.register(Identifier, AbstractTexture) and remove with release(Identifier).

claims.claim: (5) BlockEntityRenderer uses a render-state API with submit(state, PoseStack, SubmitNodeCollector, CameraRenderState), and a fullbright textured quad can be drawn with it.
claims.detail: The interface is BlockEntityRenderer<T extends BlockEntity, S extends BlockEntityRenderState>. Methods: S createRenderState(); default extractRenderState(T blockEntity, S state, float partialTicks, Vec3 cameraPosition, ModelFeatureRenderer.CrumblingOverlay breakProgress); submit(S state, PoseStack poseStack, SubmitNodeCollector submitNodeCollector, CameraRenderState camera), with CameraRenderState in net.minecraft.client.renderer.state.level; plus shouldRenderOffScreen(), getViewDistance() and shouldRender(T, Vec3). Register with BlockEntityRenderers.register(type, ctx -> ...), which Fabric transitive access wideners expose; Fabric's BlockEntityRendererRegistry is @Deprecated. For a fullbright quad, copy vanilla MapRenderer: `collector.submitCustomGeometry(poseStack, RenderTypes.text(textureId), (pose, vc) -> vc.addVertex(pose,x,y,z).setColor(-1).setUv(u,v).setLight(LightCoordsUtil.FULL_BRIGHT))` four times. LightCoordsUtil.FULL_BRIGHT = 15728880. Entity renderers use the same submit signature, and submitNameTag(PoseStack, Vec3, int offset, Component, boolean seeThrough, int lightCoords, CameraRenderState) exists.
claims.source: client.jar BlockEntityRenderer, OrderedSubmitNodeCollector, RenderTypes, LightCoordsUtil, MapRenderer; fabric-api 26.3 BlockEntityRendererRegistry.java

claims.claim: (6) 26.3 replaced GLFW with SDL3, and Screen input event signatures changed.
claims.detail: No lwjgl-glfw library and zero org/lwjgl/glfw references; input uses lwjgl-sdl 3.4.3. GuiEventListener signatures: keyPressed(KeyEvent event), keyReleased(KeyEvent), charTyped(CharacterEvent event), preeditUpdated(PreeditEvent), mouseClicked(MouseButtonEvent event, boolean doubleClick), mouseReleased(MouseButtonEvent), mouseDragged(MouseButtonEvent event, double dx, double dy), mouseScrolled(double x, double y, double scrollX, double scrollY), and mouseMoved(double x, double y). KeyEvent(int key, int keycode, int modifiers) is built from SDL_KeyboardEvent.scancode(), key() and mod(), so key is the SDL scancode. InputConstants: KEY_A=4, KEY_RETURN=40, KEY_ESCAPE=41, KEY_BACKSPACE=42, KEY_LCONTROL=224, KEY_LSHIFT=225, MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT=1, MIDDLE=2, RIGHT=3, MOD_SHIFT=3, MOD_CONTROL=192, MOD_ALT=768, MOD_SUPER=3072. CharacterEvent(int codepoint) carries no modifiers; characters come only from SDL text-input events, which require Minecraft.getInstance().onTextInputFocusChange(listener, true) (SDL_StartTextInput). Gui.setScreen calls stopTextInput() on screen changes. Open screens with Minecraft.getInstance().gui.setScreen(s); Minecraft.setScreen no longer exists.

claims.claim: (7) What --quickPlaySingleplayer does when the world folder is missing.
claims.detail: QuickPlay.joinSingleplayerWorld: if !levelSource.levelExists(id), it calls gui.setScreen(new DisconnectedScreen(new SelectWorldScreen(new TitleScreen()), 'quickplay.error.title' ("Failed to Quick Play"), 'quickplay.error.invalid_identifier' ("Could not find a world with the provided identifier"), 'gui.toWorld')). It never creates a world. A blank id uses getLatestSingleplayerWorld, and cancelling openWorld goes to the TitleScreen.

claims.claim: (9a) Fake player skins can be set with an unsigned GameProfile textures property.
claims.detail: GameProfile is record(UUID id, String name, PropertyMap properties), and PropertyMap is immutable (ImmutableMultimap.copyOf). Build it as `new GameProfile(uuid, name, new PropertyMap(ImmutableMultimap.of("textures", new Property("textures", value, signature))))`. authlib marks unsigned textures as SignatureState.UNSIGNED. However, PlayerInfo.createSkinLookup uses SkinManager.createLookup(profile, requireSecure = !minecraft.isLocalPlayer(id)), so non-local players with insecure skins fall back to the default skin. Use a signed value and signature pair (for example from a real or MineSkin-generated profile), or a client mixin on PlayerInfo.getSkin() or AbstractClientPlayer.getSkin() that returns PlayerSkin.insecure(...) with a locally registered texture. Texture URLs must also pass authlib's discovery-service allowlist (isAllowedTextureDomain); behaviour in offline mode is unverified.
claims.source: authlib-10.0.77.jar (GameProfile, PropertyMap, MinecraftServicesSessionService.unpackTextures); client.jar PlayerInfo.createSkinLookup, SkinManager, PlayerSkin

claims.claim: (9b) Fake players can be hidden from the tab list.
claims.detail: This is possible, but only with a mixin. ClientboundPlayerInfoUpdatePacket.Entry(ServerPlayer) hard-codes listed=true, and the packet has no public way to send listed=false. The client requires PlayerInfo before spawning a player entity ("Server attempted to add player prior to sending player info"), so a REMOVE packet would stop the agent from rendering. Options: mixin the Entry constructor to set listed=false for agents (Action.UPDATE_LISTED exists), or a client mixin filtering PlayerTabOverlay.getPlayerInfos() / ClientPacketListener.getListedOnlinePlayers(). ServerPlayer.allowsListing() only affects the server-status sample.

claims.claim: (10) 26.3 added a vanilla cushion entity that players sit on, usable for chairs.
claims.detail: The class is net.minecraft.world.entity.decoration.Cushion extends BlockAttachedEntity, registered as EntityTypes.CUSHION (entity type constants moved from EntityType to EntityTypes). It comes in 16 dye colours via DATA_COLOR. interact(Player, InteractionHand, Vec3): if !player.isSecondaryUseActive() && !isVehicle(), the server calls player.startRiding(this), plays SoundEvents.CUSHION_SIT and returns SUCCESS_SERVER. Entity.canAddPassenger defaults to passengers.isEmpty(), giving one rider unless startRiding(e, force=true, ...) is used. The cushion only survives with a block anchor below it (wouldSurviveAt/hasAnchorBelow) and breaks in fire. The wiki says it is not experimental, only players sit, and seated riders ignore knockback and portals. The wiki's 'dismount by using again' is not verified in code; stopRiding or sneaking works.

designImplications: Toolchain: install a JDK 25 (Temurin 25) and use Gradle 9.7.1 with Loom 1.18.x (or 1.18-SNAPSHOT), MC 26.3, loader 0.19.5 and Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3 (or 0.162.0+26.3). Loom 1.18 is Java-25 bytecode, so the Gradle daemon must run on JDK 25. The local Temurin 17 is not enough. Mojang's java-runtime-epsilon includes javac, but using it as JAVA_HOME for Gradle is untested.

Agent bodies: copy Carpet v26.3's pattern (MIT) rather than depending on all of Carpet. That means a Connection subclass with an accessor mixin for the Netty channel, a PlayerList mixin that swaps in a custom ServerGamePacketListenerImpl, and the action-pack tick mixin. Override die() to run MineVibe's agent-death logic: drop loot, disconnect, delete the agent's playerdata, and issue a fresh UUID so the death is permanent.

Seats: put a vanilla Cushion entity (EntityTypes.CUSHION) on each desk's seat block. Seat agents with non-forced fake.startRiding(cushion) or with the USE action on the cushion entity, so canAddPassenger enforces one occupant. Do not use Carpet's mount(), which forces the ride and bypasses that check. To kick an agent, call agent.stopRiding() on the server.

Hardcore reset: detect the host ServerPlayer's death on the server (ServerLivingEntityEvents.ALLOW_DEATH/AFTER_DEATH, excluding fakes) and suppress the vanilla DeathScreen with a client mixin. Then, on the client thread: disconnect to a GenericMessageScreen (this blocks until the server thread exits), deleteLevel() via LevelStorageSource.createAccess, and createFreshLevel(newId, hardcore DifficultySettings, WorldOptions.defaultWithRandomSeed(), WorldPresets::createNormalWorldDimensions, fallback). Agent memory and PC sandboxes are kept or wiped by the Node server, not by the world save.

Startup: --quickPlaySingleplayer shows an error screen when the world is missing, so either the launcher passes it only for a world that exists, or the mod intercepts the first TitleScreen (or DisconnectedScreen) and calls openWorld or createFreshLevel itself. Keep the 'current world id' in a MineVibe config file.

Monitor rendering: decode JPEG with STBImage.stbi_load_from_memory into a NativeImage(Format.RGBA, w, h, true, ptr), or have Node send raw RGBA. Upload dirty rects on the render thread with CommandEncoder.writeToTexture(GpuTexture, ByteBuffer, 0, 0, x, y, w, h). Draw with submitCustomGeometry and RenderTypes.text(id) plus LightCoordsUtil.FULL_BRIGHT, as vanilla MapRenderer does. Subclass DynamicTexture to set a LINEAR clamp-to-edge sampler. Use only the com.mojang.renderpearl API (no raw GL) so the experimental Vulkan backend keeps working.

PC input screen: on open, call Minecraft.getInstance().onTextInputFocusChange(screen, true) so charTyped events arrive. Forward KeyEvent.key() (SDL scancode) through an SDL-scancode-to-X11/cua key table, and send text from CharacterEvent codepoints. Mouse buttons are 1/2/3. Override keyPressed fully so Tab and Escape go to the PC, and reserve Shift+Esc to release control. Return false from isPauseScreen().

Skins and tab list: render agent skins with a client mixin on PlayerInfo.getSkin()/AbstractClientPlayer.getSkin() returning PlayerSkin.insecure(...) with locally registered textures; unsigned profile textures are ignored for remote players. Hide agents from the tab list by forcing Entry.listed=false or filtering on the client. Never send a REMOVE packet, because the agent would stop rendering.

Node launcher: use the @xmcl/installer 6.x workflow API (createFabricInstallWorkflow, the resolve*InstallFiles functions and executeInstallManifest) plus createJavaRuntimeInstallWorkflow with the all.json entry for mac-os-arm64 / java-runtime-epsilon. Launch with @xmcl/core using javaPath=<dest>/jre.bundle/Contents/Home/bin/java, offline gameProfile, quickPlaySingleplayer, and extraJVMArgs for the WebSocket token. Do not use MCLC.

26.x API renames to expect in code: Identifier (not ResourceLocation); EntityTypes.* and BlockEntityTypes.* constants; Gui.setScreen; GuiGraphicsExtractor/extractRenderState; LevelRenderEvents; PayloadTypeRegistry.clientboundPlay()/serverboundPlay(); GameProfile and Property are records.
